messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the console rollout at 10:12 UTC we started seeing ~2% of WS connections become "silent": socket stays ESTABLISHED but client gets no messages for 30-90s. Repro on canary and eu-prod.

maria: sample client log: `WS open -> subscribe(route_id=shipping-events) -> no frames for 42s -> reconnect`. No 5xx in ingress, just no frames.

ajay: Seen it too. Was routing policy changed during the rollout? we flipped `route_preference=latency_first` -> `cost_aware` yesterday.

kevin: Not that setting directly. We did change the per-tenant rate limiter to sliding-window 1s buckets for streaming fanout to reduce token spikes. Could be interaction with backpressure.

ops-bot: alert: streaming-fanout-silent-connections spike at 2026-03-18T10:14:23Z (+37s) — samples: tenant=acme, route=shipping-events, proxy=eu-ws-2

ben: Is this quota throttling or proxy backpressure? initial hypothesis: proxy has internal queue overflow and drops frames silently.

maria: Console telemetry shows route-level outgoing frames dropped metric didn't spike. But connection-level `idle_frame_duration` did. The console per-route breakdown seems to undercount dropped frames for routes that were rebalanced mid-rollout. (Screenshot: https://console.internal/shot/8672)

zara: If console undercounts, that explains product confused customers. We rolled out the new per-route quota view — could be a backend aggregation window mismatch.

ajay: Quick reproduction: run a 200-client fanout to the route with low token gen. Most clients get steady frames, a few hang exactly at ~42s consistently. Attaching the minimal repro script:
```
# stress-ws.sh (pseudo)
for i in {1..200}; do
  node ws-client.js --route shipping-events &
done
```

kevin: Can you dump the proxy logs for one of the stuck connections? look for `queue_full` / `kvcache_fallthrough` markers. I suspect our sliding-window limiter enters a transient state where it signals downstream to pause but proxy never resumes push.

maria: Pasted proxy excerpt: `ctx=conn-9723 route=shipping-events state=paused cause=rate-window` then nothing until client reconnect. No resume event logged.

ajay: That smells like a bug in the resume/fallback path: when route ownership flips during rollout, the resume-token isn't propagated so handler never receives unpause.

kevin: Confirmed a few code paths only emit `resume` on `route_owner == true`. During migration there's a small window where owner==false and we drop resume events. Fix candidate: emit resume to the connection manager independent of owner flag (with idempotency guard).

zara: How risky is that change for latencies? we can't cause additional CPU churn in hot paths during peak.

kevin: Minimal. It's a simple enqueue of a resume event; worst-case we do a no-op. Will add a unit test for idempotency and a perf microbenchmark.

ben: For short term mitigation, can we revert the per-tenant sliding-window limiter or widen the window?

ajay: We can widen to 2s buckets without major cost hit. I'll open a canary config change for eu-prod only.

maria: Also, we need console fix: per-route aggregation currently uses a 10s tumbling window while backend uses 1s sliding. That mismatch makes dropped frames look rare.

zara: Filed REDWOOD-UI-224: align aggregation windows + add a note in the rollout playbook.

kevin: I'll prepare a PR to emit resume events unconditionally with idempotency. Target: hotfix branch, rollout to canary, monitor `idle_frame_duration` and `resume_sent` counters.

maria: After ajay widened window on canary -> silent connections dropped to 0.6% from 2%. Good mitigation.

ben: Next steps: (1) kevin hotfix PR, (2) ajay config widen on prod schedule, (3) zara console aggregation fix, (4) add alert for `conn_paused_without_resume > 5m`.

ajay: I'll schedule the config change in the next 30m and roll to us-west -> eu-prod.

kevin: PR ready, running unit tests locally, will push in 15.

maria: Thanks — keeping watch on the canary dashboards. If anyone sees a recurrence ping here. :thumbsup:
